script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 21. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Watch a team that trusts each other—they move fast, communicate effortlessly, take risks.  Watch a team without trust—every decision requires checking, verifying, protecting.  Trust is invisible infrastructure.

Low-trust environments require contracts, oversight, verification—all expensive. High-trust environments move faster with less friction. Trust isn't just nice; it's economically essential. Organizations with high trust outperform by wide margins. Research shows trust often starts with vulnerability—someone takes a risk first.  Leaders who admit mistakes create trust faster than those who seem perfect.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Trust is built in drops and lost in buckets.  Consistency over time creates reliability.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Trust Deposit - Be Consistent.

Here's your activity: Identify one relationship where you want more trust. What consistent action could you take daily or weekly to build it? Trust is an account—make small deposits regularly. One kept promise at a time. This helps you build trust through reliability.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about trust and teams can be applied to trust deposit - be consistent. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
